subject: Deployment mode & migration follow-up - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novahealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Discovery call recap - deployment modes and migration

Hi Samir / Alex - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps.

Call summary:
- Current environment: you're running a mix of an external LLM API and in-house GPU clusters (legacy), with recent spikes in latency and higher-than-expected token costs.
- Key requirements: predictable latency for low-latency endpoints, data residency for PHI-adjacent datasets, SOC2 evidence for procurement, and a predictable pricing band for forecasting.
- Migration drivers: reduce per-token cost, simplify ops, and consolidate observability.

Deployment options we discussed (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, no infra to manage; good if data residency & audit needs can be met via contract + VPC peering patterns.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools we operate for you - predictable throughput and isolation, SLA-backed.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full customer-managed networking and optional on-prem package for regulated workloads.

As promised, I've attached a short overview (redwood-deployment-options.pdf) that maps these options to common migration patterns.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you share the procurement timeline and any mandatory controls (e.g., SOC2, specific retention windows)?
2) If helpful, I can loop in our Solutions Engineer (Dev Patel) for a technical migration plan.
3) After we align on controls and capacity needs, we'll put together a mutual action plan (MAP) and a rough SOW.

Would you be available for a 30-minute tech sync next week? If so, tell me preferred times and I'll coordinate.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(650) 555-0183

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side:

- Residency/compliance: Nova Health needs audit logs + SOC2 evidence. We also have an EU patient data subset that needs to stay in-region for now (so a hybrid requirement). Is that supported by Hosted + VPC peering or do we need Private for EU data?
- Performance: our worst-case 95p latency target is < 200ms for small-chat endpoints - we're willing to pay more for predictability. Can Dedicated meet that consistently?
- Migration effort: are you able to support mapping our existing prompts and chat flows from the other API (we currently use a mix of OpenAI-compatible endpoints and an internal caching layer)? We'd like a rough estimate of engineering effort and any assistance you provide.
- Timeline: procurement aims to finish vendor selection by 8/15.

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@novahealth.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Fwd: RE: Discovery call recap - deployment modes and migration (please advise)

Hi Samir / Marissa - thanks for the details and for scheduling the tech sync. High-level technical recommendations below; happy to go deeper on Wed 7/15.

Short answer: all three deployment modes are viable depending on constraints. Recommended sequence to minimize risk: Hosted (test) -> Dedicated pilot -> Private for regulated EU subset if required.

Why this sequence:
- Hosted API: fastest way to validate prompts and request/response behavior with minimal infra changes. We can use isolated projects and strict logging controls to capture audit evidence during pilot. Not ideal if you must guarantee EU-only processing in production.
- Dedicated: gives you predictable throughput and lower variance in latency (SLA-backed). Dedicated infra can be pinned to a region and sized to meet your 95p < 200ms target (we typically recommend reserved capacity sized for peak concurrency + x1.5).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): required when legal/regulatory controls demand customer-managed networking or air-gapped processing. This is heavier lift but we provide an on-prem package and playbooks for cutover.

Migration checklist (proposed):
1) Export representative API logs and prompt samples (we need examples of 1) average token lengths, 2) peak concurrency windows, 3) model variants in use).
2) Canonicalize prompts + create automated prompt test harnesses (so we can track regressions).
3) Pilot in Hosted with telemetry and prefix caching enabled (2-3 weeks).
4) Dedicated pilot (3-4 weeks) with load testing and SLA validation.
5) If EU subset requires private processing, deploy Private for that region and configure routing policies for EU traffic.

Estimated timeline: 6-8 weeks from initial pilot to production cutover (Hosted->Dedicated), additional 4-6 weeks if Private region deploy is required.

Ballpark cost considerations: pilot Hosted usage minimal (trial credits), Dedicated pilot (small pool) O(USD 10-25k/month depending on GPU class), Private on-prem adds professional services and infra costs - we'll provide a firm estimate after we see logs and target concurrency.

Data residency & SOC2: Redwood provides SOC2 Type II reports and audit logs for all deployment modes. For strict EU-only processing, Private (VPC or on-prem) is the straightforward route; Dedicated can be region-pinned but requires contractual assurances - we can include those in the MAP.

Next steps I need from Nova Health before Wed:
- Sample API logs (anonymized is fine) and a short doc with peak concurrency and model sizes.
- Confirmation whether the EU subset must be physically separated in production (yes/no).

Scheduling: book a 30-min technical sync here: https://meetings.redwood.com/dev-patel/30min

Happy to put together a draft SOW and MAP once we have logs.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
